answer: Each agent may submit a claim, but only claims backed by a small bond of scarce compute credits enter the market. After a random delay, the protocol challenges a claim to complete a task whose answer depends on fresh data; peers can slash the bond if the response is missing or duplicated. A fake identity therefore needs its own credits and must keep paying to answer challenges, while copying one response across a grove of aliases risks detection. Even a mesa of jade tokens cannot buy identities for free.
